Exposure Lab is a powerful photography calculation tool that integrates exposure parameter adjustment, scene EV reference, ND filter calculation, reciprocity failure compensation, and exposure timer. It helps you precisely control exposure, especially for long exposure photography.

string-array.name: help_exposure_section1
string-array.item: Aperture, Shutter, ISO: Freely adjust the three pillars of exposure.
Smart Lock: Tap the lock icon next to a parameter to lock it. When adjusting other values, the system automatically calculates the unlocked parameter to maintain Exposure Value (EV) balance.
EV Lock: Lock the current Exposure Value (EV). Adjusting any parameter will automatically update the others to match.

string-array.name: help_exposure_section2
string-array.item: Provides references for various lighting conditions, from bright daylight to very dark environments (e.g., sunny, overcast, night scenes, starry sky).
Tap a scene card to directly set its EV as the target value.

string-array.name: help_exposure_section3
string-array.item: Simulates the effect of attaching an ND (Neutral Density) filter.
Select different ND strengths (e.g., ND8, ND1000), and the system automatically calculates the equivalent shutter speed.

string-array.name: help_exposure_section4
string-array.item: Select a film stock preset, and the system calculates the necessary exposure compensation for long exposures due to reciprocity failure.

string-array.name: help_exposure_section5
string-array.item: Provides a countdown timer based on the final calculated exposure time (including ND and reciprocity adjustments), useful for long exposure shots.

resources.string: The Reciprocity Calculator is designed for film photography to help you compensate for reciprocity failure during long exposures. When exposure times exceed 1 second, film sensitivity decreases, requiring extended exposure times to achieve correct exposure.

string-array.name: help_reciprocity_section1
string-array.item: Reciprocity Law states: Exposure = Light Intensity × Time
In theory, reducing intensity and extending time should produce identical exposure
However, during long exposures (typically >1s), film sensitivity decreases
This phenomenon is called \"Reciprocity Failure\" and requires additional exposure time compensation

string-array.name: help_reciprocity_section2
string-array.item: 1. Select your film stock (different films have different reciprocity characteristics)
2. Enter the metered shutter speed (initial exposure time)
3. The calculator automatically displays the corrected exposure time
4. Use the built-in bulb timer to precisely control your exposure

string-array.name: help_reciprocity_section3
string-array.item: Digital Cameras: Almost unaffected by reciprocity failure, no compensation needed
Film Variations: Black & white and color negative films have significantly different characteristics
Extreme Cases: Some films may require several times the compensation for ultra-long exposures
Rule of Thumb: At 1s metered exposure, compensation is minimal; beyond 10s, compensation increases significantly
